chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The wedding feast (walimah) on the first day is a right (Sunnah), and the second day is goodness (recommended), and whatever is added beyond that is for show-off and fame.'

key_terms.الْوَلِيمَةُ: The wedding feast or banquet hosted by the groom's family
key_terms.حَقٌّ: A right or confirmed Sunnah, indicating a strong recommendation
key_terms.رِيَاءٌ: Show-off or performing deeds for the sake of being seen by others
key_terms.سُمْعَةٌ: Fame or seeking reputation and public attention
key_terms.مَعْرُوفٌ: Goodness or a recommended act, less obligatory than 'haqq'

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the duration and purpose of the wedding feast (walimah)?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to guide the community against the cultural excesses of his time, distinguishing between religious obligation, social courtesy, and vanity. This tripartite structure emphasizes that while the initial celebration is a communal duty, prolonged feasting for the sake of display is discouraged as a spiritual flaw. It reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing social joy with sincerity (ikhlas) and moderation in financial expenditure.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘
The Waleema (Wedding feast) on the first day is true (Sunnah), and the second (day) it is goodness, and whatever is an increase is a show-off and to be heard of’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
Serving food in a wedding ceremony for the first day is a right, the second day is reasonable, and for more than this is a show-off and publicity.’”
